features_off.opendal-fs: on at the deltalake-opendal level, where it is a default
features_off.opendal-memory: on at the deltalake-opendal level, where it is a default

features_off.delta-cache: zero cfg(feature) sites in crates/core/src; pulls foyer and tempfile for no item surface
features_off.datafusion-ext: an alias for `datafusion`, which is on; enabling it changes no cfg
features_off.humantime: optional dependency of cloud, which is on; the feature itself is not a cfg gate

deltalake-core.note: 127 cfg(feature = "datafusion") sites -- this is the feature that decides whether the DataFusion seam exists at all. 54 nanosecond-timestamps sites, of which 4 are not(feature = ...), so enabling it removes a small amount of surface as well as adding a large amount.

deltalake-aws.note: zero cfg(feature) sites in src: the documented surface is complete regardless of the tls choice

deltalake-hdfs.note: zero cfg(feature) sites in src; backed by pure-Rust hdfs-native-object-store, so no JVM or libhdfs is involved

deltalake-mount.note: documented as a crate although the deltalake facade has no `mount` feature and does not re-export it: reachable only by depending on deltalake-mount directly

features_off.opendal-s3: every opendal-* service feature gates only a register_handlers arm; none adds an item
features_off.opendal-ftp: service registration only; native FTP dependency
features_off.opendal-sftp: service registration only; native libssh2 dependency

deltalake-catalog-unity.note: the only backend crate with real cfg gating: aws/azure/gcp/r2 have 5 sites each and datafusion 3, and several are not(feature = ...) variants, so enabling all four removes those alternatives

features_off.declarative-plans: experimental; not enabled by delta-rs and needs prost-build
features_off.test-utils: not enabled by delta-rs; would expose test-only constructors as public
features_off.column-defaults-in-dev: in-progress work; not enabled by delta-rs

buoyant_kernel.note: Documented under delta-rs's OWN unified feature selection, by naming it with -p inside the delta-rs workspace, not as a separate build. That is deliberate: an all-features kernel would advertise items a deltalake user cannot reach. internal-api (47 cfg sites) flips crc, column_trie, utils, path and log_replay from pub(crate) to pub, and delta-rs relies on that.
